circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has served as the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue following Bahrain's establishment, with Qatar and Saudi Arabia subsequently joining the calendar.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Australian Grand Prix as part of Formula One's calendar alongside supporting Supercars and lower-tier racing categories. The venue maintains an FIA Grade 1 classification for international motorsport competition.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following extensive modification and renaming, the track returned to hosting the race from 1997 to 2003 in its redesigned configuration.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street course in Azerbaijan's capital that stretches 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest track in Formula One competition. The venue first hosted a grand prix in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards, operated by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that year. The FIA Grade 1-licensed venue accommodates various motorsports including GP2 racing, endurance competitions, and features multiple track configurations for different racing series.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit is renowned as a versatile test of driving skill, featuring an assortment of corner types alongside extended straights. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This Belgian circuit near Spa covers 7. 004 km and has been a Formula One venue since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. It hosted the first Grand Prix at the track in 1925 and has regularly featured on the F1 calendar annually since 1985, with only 2003 and 2006 as exceptions.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve spans 4. 361 kilometers and serves as the permanent home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its primary use for Formula One racing, the venue has accommodated various international motorsporting competitions including sports car championships and North American open-wheel and stock car series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit is a motorsport venue renowned for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran from 2004 to 2019 before returning in 2024. The track has expanded its racing calendar to include additional international motorsport events alongside the Formula One championship.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, this English circuit inaugurated the British Grand Prix in 1948 and later hosted the maiden World Championship race in 1950. After alternating venues with Aintree and Brands Hatch for three decades, the British Grand Prix became a permanent fixture here from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other F1 venue, the track was constructed outside the city near a major road after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected by the government.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Monza north of Milan, the Autodromo Nazionale is a 5. 793 km track established in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit. It has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, earning the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its characteristic long straights and rapid corners designed to produce high-velocity racing.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture that serves as a primary racing hub for Formula One and Super Formula competitions. Operated by Honda Mobilityland and accommodating 155,000 spectators, the track has established itself as one of the sport's most prestigious venues.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, along the famous Las Vegas Boulevard where major hotels and casinos are situated. The layout winds past iconic venues including MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, integrating the city's most recognizable landmarks into the racing track itself.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit in Mexico City honoring brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents. The venue has hosted the Mexican Grand Prix multiple times across different track configurations, most recently from 2015 onwards under its current Mexico City Grand Prix designation, following a 23-year absence from the Formula One calendar.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that stretches 3. 363 miles with 19 corners, allowing Formula One cars to average approximately 139 mph during qualifying. Designed specifically by renowned circuit architects Apex Circuit Design, the venue became the home of the Miami Grand Prix when it joined the championship calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco winds through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine in the Principality of Monaco, spanning 3. 337 km around the harbour. The track is widely known as "Monte Carlo" due to its location predominantly within that district of Monaco.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the 4. 259 km Zandvoort circuit made its Formula One comeback in 2021 when the Dutch Grand Prix was revived at the venue. The track will host the race through 2026, after which its partnership with the championship concludes.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Lusail International Circuit is situated north of Doha in Qatar and stretches 5. 419 kilometers with a primary straightaway spanning 1. 068 kilometers.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically died in a 1977 aircraft accident. The counterclockwise track hosts major international motorsport events and features an adjacent kart facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street-based racing venue positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has hosted the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since 2021. The track also began accommodating international electric racing competition from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang planning areas into its layout as a street-based racing venue.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced layout combining extended straightaways with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that annually hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside other major motorsport events including NASCAR and MotoGP competition. The venue has established itself as a premier racing destination in North America, having previously accommodated various international racing series before becoming a cornerstone event on the F1 calendar.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver currently representing Thailand on the Formula One grid with Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spain's Fernando Alonso represents Aston Martin on the current Formula One grid, having claimed two world titles during his 23-season career with 32 race victories to his name. Beyond single-seaters, he has achieved remarkable success in endurance motorsport, capturing the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship and multiple prestigious 24-hour race victories, making him the sole driver to secure championships in both Formula One and World Endurance competition.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, an Italian driver, joined Mercedes for his Formula One debut in 2025 and has already claimed six Grand Prix victories in the championship.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: British driver Oliver Bearman currently races for Haas in Formula One, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabriel Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as part of the Audi racing program.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing experience from a 13-season career that includes 10 Grand Prix victories. He achieved back-to-back runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while driving for Mercedes in 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve position with Haas while competing in prototype sports car racing for Nielsen Racing in the European Le Mans Series. He made seven Formula One starts across the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently competing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri remains a significant highlight of his racing career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, representing France in international competition.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently competing for Ferrari who has achieved seven world championship titles, equaling Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple circuit records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing with him a distinguished endurance racing record that includes victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc represents Monaco in Formula One racing and drives for Ferrari, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career. He finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship, demonstrating his competitive performance with the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who contested Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024. Currently, he competes as a factory BMW driver in the World Endurance Championship with WRT while maintaining a part-time NASCAR presence with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British competitor in Formula One, secured the 2025 drivers' championship while racing for McLaren after accumulating 13 Grand Prix victories over his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, who previously achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez, a Mexican competitor, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One. The experienced driver finished second in the 2023 championship while with Red Bull and has claimed six race victories throughout his 15-season career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian Formula One driver currently racing for McLaren, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-season career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One spanning from 2011 through 2024 and secured eight Grand Prix victories during his 14-season career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has claimed seven victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four race victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition. After competing in Formula One during 2023 and 2024, he has transitioned to sports car racing, having previously driven in IMSA's LMP2 class for Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver who currently races for Aston Martin in the sport's top series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda has been active in Formula One since 2021, currently functioning as a reserve driver for both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls through 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian competitor has achieved four consecutive world championship victories between 2021 and 2024 while driving for Red Bull Racing, accumulating 71 Grand Prix wins throughout his 12-season Formula One career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a Formula One driver currently fulfilling a reserve role with Cadillac. He competed in the sport's top tier from 2022 through 2024, holding the distinction of being the sole Chinese national to have raced in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, continuing Renault's factory Formula One presence until the manufacturer's withdrawal at the end of 2025. Operating with a French racing license and powered by Mercedes engines, Alpine's only victory came through Esteban Ocon's triumph at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has maintained a presence in Formula One through different organizational structures, with the modern iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the Italian automotive manufacturer's Formula One racing operation and stands as both the championship's longest-continuous competitor and its most accomplished team since 1950. The squad, nicknamed after its distinctive horse emblem, has maintained an unbroken presence throughout the sport's entire modern history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with the outfit entering the sport in 2016. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, Ayao Komatsu has assumed the role of team principal.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering and racing enterprise established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, the outfit initially competed in endurance racing before joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent chassis manufacturer. Operating continuously through various ownership changes, it became one of the sport's longest-serving constructors before concluding its final season in 2025, at which point Audi acquired the team's operational structure and assets to establish its own F1 program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under corporate sponsorship. The team operates as part of the wider McLaren Group, with ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes-AMG Petronas operates as a Formula One team from its Brackley base since Mercedes first entered the sport in 1954, competing under a German licence. The squad gained additional ownership from Ineos in 2022, joining existing stakeholders Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff in a tripartite structure. Historically recognized as the "Silver Arrows," Mercedes has maintained a dominant presence as both engine supplier and team operator throughout the championship's modern era.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024, operating as a second team under Red Bull's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with facilities in Milton Keynes, the squad functions as a sister team within the Red Bull motorsport structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned teams alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's second constructor entry in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence from their English base, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 and has become one of two top-tier teams owned by Red Bull GmbH. Christian Horner led the organization from its inception until early 2025, when Laurent Mekies assumed the leadership role.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, emerging from Williams's previous unsuccessful racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and operates from a substantial facility in the English Midlands.
